main_text.p: wrote Zoroaster, the son of Armenius, by race a Pamphylian, having been dead in the war, which I learned of the Gods, being in Hades," as Clemens Alexandrinus relateth in the fifth book of his Stromata: where he also noteth, that this Zoroaster is that Er, the son of Armenius, a Pamphylian, of whom Plato writeth in the tenth book of his Commonwealth; that being slain in the war he revived the twelfth day after, and was sent back as a messenger to report unto men here the things which he had heard and seen in the other world; one part of whose relation was this, that he saw certain gulfsPlato, lib. 10. de repub. op. tom. 2. pag. 614. beneath in the earth, and above in the heaven, opposite one to the other, and that the just were commanded by the Judges that sat betwixt those gulfs, to go to the right hand up toward heaven, but the wicked to the left hand and downward; which testimonies EusebiusEuseb. Præpar. Evang. lib. 11. pag. 563. bringeth in, among many others, to shew the consent that is betwixt Plato and the Hebrews in matters that concern the state of the world to come.
Next to Zoroaster cometh Pythagoras: whose golden verses are concluded with this distich:

p.i: Ἡνί δ' ἀπολείψας σῶμα, ἐς αἰθέρ' ἐλεύθερον ἔλθῃς, Ἔσσεαι ἀθάνατος θεὸς, ἄμβροτος, οὐκ ἔτι θνητός.

main_text.p: "When thou shalt leave the body, and come unto a free heaven, thou shalt be an immortal God, incorruptible, and not subject to mortality any more." So Epicharmus the scholar of Pythagoras: "IfΕὐσεβὴς νῷ πεφυκώς, οὐ πάθοις γ' οὐδὲν κακὸν καταθανὼν· ἄνω τὸ πνεῦμα διαμένει κατ' οὐρανόν. thou be godly in mind, thou shalt suffer no evil when thou art dead; thy spirit shall
πολέμῳ τελευτήσας, ὅσα ἐν ᾅδῃ γενόμενος ἰδὰην παρὰ θεῶν. Zoroaster, apud Clem. Alexandr. lib. 5. Stromat. indeque apud Euseb. præpar. Evang. lib. 13. pag. 675.
p Plato, lib. 10. de repub. op. tom. 2. pag. 614.
q Euseb. Præpar. Evang. lib. 11. pag. 563. Vide et Origenem contra Celsum, lib. 2. pag. 72. edit. Græc.
r Pythagor. aur. Carm. cum commentar. Hieroclis, pag. 14.
s Εὐσεβὴς νῷ πεφυκώς, οὐ πάθοις γ' οὐδὲν κακὸν καταθανὼν· ἄνω τὸ πνεῦμα διαμένει κατ' οὐρανόν. Epicharm. apud Clement. Alexandr. lib. 4. Stromat.

page.notes: The footnote marks r and s in the text: "r" is not visibly placed in the body; the mark "s" follows "If". Greek in the footnotes and distich is transcribed as printed; the epigraph line of the distich may contain minor letter uncertainties.
